[[File:Boyd Orr Building.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The [[Robertson Centre for Biostatistics]] is in the [[Boyd Orr Building]], [[University of Glasgow]]]]
'''Ian Ford''' is a Scottish doctor who is a professor of [[biostatistics]] and a director of the [[Robertson Centre for Biostatistics]], and a former [[Dean of Faculty]] of Information and Mathematical Sciences, at the [[University of Glasgow]].

== Biography ==
Ford was born in Glasgow and educated at the former [[Hamilton Academy]]. He studied at the [[University of Glasgow]], graduating with a BSc and in 1976, was awarded a [[PhD]] in Statistics. From 1976-77, he was visiting Lecturer to the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]] and since then successively [[Lecturer]], Senior Lecturer, [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]], Personal Professor and [[Professor]] at the University of Glasgow.<ref name="frost">[http://www.martinfrost.ws/htmlfiles/mfwhoswho/individuals/F_mfwwi/ian_ford.html Frost’s Scottish Who’s Who – Ian Ford] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110619133803/http://martinfrost.ws/htmlfiles/mfwhoswho/individuals/F_mfwwi/ian_ford.html |date=19 June 2011 }} Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref> He is the first holder of the Chair of Biostatistics at the University.<ref>[http://www.universitystory.gla.ac.uk/biography/?id=WH2148&type=P University of Glasgow Story] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120310080913/http://www.universitystory.gla.ac.uk/biography/?id=WH2148&type=P |date=10 March 2012 }}, Universitystory.gla.ac.uk Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref>

Ford has been the Director of the [[Robertson Centre for Biostatistics]] since 1991<ref>[http://www.rcb.gla.ac.uk/contacts.htm Robertson Centre for Biostatics - staff list] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111003043749/http://www.rcb.gla.ac.uk/contacts.htm |date=3 October 2011 }}, Rcb.gla.ac.uk, Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref> and Director of the Glasgow Clinical Trials Unit. He is also a member of the editorial boards for the international journals, ''Statistical Methods for Medical Research'';<ref>[http://smm.sagepub.com Publication information - journal, 'Statistical Methods for Medical Research], Sagepub.com, Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref> ''Journal of Evaluation in Clinical Practice''<ref>[http://www.wiley.com/bw/journal.asp?ref=1356-1294 Publication information - International 'Journal of Evaluation in Clinical Practice'], Wiley.com, Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref> and ''Public Library of Science Medicine''.<ref>[http://www.plosmedicine.org/static/edboard.action Public Library of Science Medicine - international editorial board members], Plosmedicine.org, Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref><ref>[http://www.plosmedicine.org/search/simpleSearch.action?from=globalSimpleSearch&filterJournals=PLoSMedicine&query=IAn+Ford&x=0&y=0 Public Library of Science Medicine Papers and Reports by Prof. Ian Ford], Plosmedicine.org, Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref> He has written numerous papers.<ref>[http://www.shift-study.com/press/SHIFT-exec.pdf Systolic Heart Failure Treatment Trial Study – co-author, Prof. Ian Ford] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100911082023/http://www.shift-study.com/press/SHIFT-exec.pdf |date=11 September 2010 }}, Shift-study.comn Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref><ref>[http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/kidney-link-to-heart-failure-risk-1.966782 Evening Times newspaper article, release of Report, co-authored by Ian Ford], Eveningtimes.co.uk, Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref><ref>[http://www.nejm.org/search?q=Iain+Ford The New England Journal of Medicine, U.S.A. - Papers and Reports by Iain Ford], Nejm.org, Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref>

In 1999, Ford was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]].<ref>[http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/fellowship/fellows.pdf Royal Society of Edinburgh - List of Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040627152829/http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/fellowship/fellows.pdf |date=27 June 2004 }} Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref> He is also a Fellow of both the [[International Statistical Institute]] and the [[Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Glasgow]].<ref>[http://www.scot-ship.ac.uk/professor-ian-ford Scottish Health Informatics Programme – biography, Ian Ford], Scot-ship.ac.uk, Retrieved 28 October 2010</ref> A member of the Cholesterol Triallists Collaboration and the Fibrinogen Studies Collaboration, Ford is also a member of the [[American Statistical Association]]; Statisticians in the Pharmaceutical Industry; the [[Drug Information Association]]; the [[Royal Statistical Society]]; and the International Society for Clinical Biostatistics.<ref>[http://www.clarify-registry.com/healthcare-professionals/clarify-information/4-executive-committee Healthcare registry] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110708162116/http://www.clarify-registry.com/healthcare-professionals/clarify-information/4-executive-committee/ |date=8 July 2011 }}, Clarify-registry.com, Retrieved 2 November 2010</ref>

From 2000–04, Ford served as Dean of the Faculty of Information and Mathematical Sciences, University of Glasgow.<ref name="frost" />
